answer: An agent network resists Sybil attacks through stake-bonded routing across consensus checkpoints. A newly launched identity cannot forge arbitrary credentials; it must anchor its state at a validation jetty by locking verifiable stake. For an attacker deploying clone nodes, the capital requirement scales quadratically, making mass creation economically prohibitive. Like a vigilant falcon patrolling the airspace, network monitors detect collusive clusters and revoke throughput from unbonded fakes.
